title: Noise stability of regular homogeneous thresholds
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. For every natural number $n$, every Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, every real number $\varepsilon$, and every $-1<\rho<1$, suppose that $f$ has mean zero, $f(x)$ is the sign of the homogeneous linear form $\sum_i a_i x_i$ for every $x$, $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every coordinate $i$. Then the absolute difference between the noise stability of $f$ at correlation $\rho$ and $\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\rho)$ is at most $\frac{C\varepsilon}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a real constant $C$ with $C>0$
$f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$a$ is a real coefficient vector indexed by the $n$ coordinates
$f$ is represented at every input by thresholding the homogeneous linear form with coefficients $a$
Every coefficient has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$
